summary: MERGE PENDING — orch/attempt/tool-usage-analytics: MCP tool-usage analytics instrumented at the single dispatch choke point (mcp-core handleRpc tools/call beacons POST /analytics/tool-call via the existing daemon-bound call client — covers BOTH stdio and HTTP transports; awaited so the stdio process can't exit before the beacon lands). New lib/analytics.js persists per-tool aggregates (total/errors/last_called/per-workspace/rolling-7d day buckets) to BASE/tool-analytics.json with a 2s debounced flush. GET /analytics/tools enumerates the full 38-tool registry (never-called = zero rows, removed tools flagged); GET /analytics serves a sorted-table dashboard page (public/analytics.html) highlighting never-called tools. Tests: 36/36 unit suites pass, smoke.sh 97/97, new test/tool-analytics.test.js 19/19; e2e verified both transports count + counters survive daemon restart. Live daemon needs a restart to pick this up after merge. Commit 9d8512f.

subject: Tool-usage analytics: instrument daemon to count every MCP tool call
description: In /Users/imyu/Desktop/cloude/orchestrator: instrument the MCP dispatch path (lib/mcp-core.js handleRpc and/or daemon.js /mcp endpoint — both stdio and HTTP transports must be covered) to record every tools/call: tool name, timestamp, workspace, success/error. Persist counters across daemon restarts (small JSON state file, append-or-aggregate; keep it cheap — no per-call disk write storms, batch/debounce flush). Expose GET /analytics/tools returning per-tool totals + last-called + 7d window counts. Add a small dashboard panel (public/) listing tools sorted by usage with a "never called" highlight. Purpose: replace grep-based audits with empirical data for tool-surface pruning. Keep it minimal — no charting library, a sorted table is enough. Note: if a PreToolUse gate blocks direct edits to orchestrator source, write to /tmp and cp into place.
